reviews.author: Sarah P.
reviews.text: I grew up on this lake and still love coming back whenever I can, it's still as beautiful as it always was.

reviews.author: vlp p.
reviews.text: Impressive due to silence outside camping season, unfortunatelly the waterlevel was far below average showing a climate  impacted scene.

reviews.author: VanTrips G.
reviews.text: A beautiful lake located along the route to Mount Rainier, near the town of Elbe. Its water comes from rivers fed by the melting snow of the mountain, making it exceptionally cold and refreshing. The lake is connected to Alder Dam, which supplies drinking water to the city of Tacoma. It’s a stunning spot for boating, kayaking, canoeing, and jet skiing.

reviews.author: Crazy B.
reviews.text: Lake is clean and have a designated area for family swimming.

reviews.author: Y.C. W.
reviews.text: It’s a beautiful park with a great view of the lake. I wish there’s a trail to walk / bike around the lake, but there’s no. If you happen to have some extra time during your trip to Mt Rainier, then you can stop by here to enjoy the beautiful view of the lake. The view of the dam is also pretty interesting.

reviews.author: James T
reviews.text: Alder Lake is a large man-made lake, created and run by a power utility. As off-putting as that may sound, it's actually a very attractive lake, with a nice camp area, sand beach for swimming, and plenty of fishing, water-sport area. We went there for a family reunion, and had a super time: we were able to get a number of adjacent campsites, reserved the large open "hall" for our family dinner, and had a nice bonfire to sit around that evening.

reviews.author: worddujour
reviews.text: 3 does, 1 buck and us - and no one else - perfection! My husband Ed & I found this Washington / Tacoma Power Company park on line and finally had a chance to stay there. It has a wonderful campground with full hook ups and huge trees for only $28. And if you're a senior, you can get a $5.00 discount! Plus gorgeous Alder Lake with swimming and water sports. All of this at the foot of Mt. Ranier !!!!

reviews.author: boat07
reviews.text: It is an average park of this kind. The area is nice and easy to find.

reviews.author: Bill M
reviews.text: Decent lake, clean and enough space for the whole family. There is even a protected area to get out of the weather if mother nature takes a turn.

reviews.author: donnay985
reviews.text: We stayed a week in our rv here...nice large site, friendly host, beautiful lake right fhere a few steps away, and two deer that must live there as well, since we saw them each day. Beautiful area.

reviews.author: stevedM8262ZC
reviews.text: This is a great campground for tent or RV camping. Very spacious camp sites, we didn't feel intruded on by other camp sites at all. But more importantly the views of Mount Rainier are exquisite. If you're fortunate enough to have a boat in which you can go out and cruise the lake you will see some of the most amazing views of the mountain. A very remote lake with excellent Kokanee, Bass, and Trout fishing. If you're a camper I highly recommend Alder Lake Park.

reviews.author: April B
reviews.text: The family and I have gone to Alder Lake for years to go boating with friends or by ourselves. We have gone all over the lake in our boat. We have played in the swimming area and gone for walks on the trails. The only negative thing I have to say is the boat launch parking lot is tiny. Many times we've pulled into the lot and see cars parked in the spots meant for truck and boat parking. During good weather, if you want to go boating get to the park early the lot fills quickly.

reviews.author: USN_Seabee_Wife
reviews.text: We really enjoy staying at this park and have done so several times. The staff is always very friendly and frequently drive around to make sure that the trash is emptied and the bathrooms are clean. We just stayed this weekend and the only downer was that there were no campfires allowed. There are also several sites that are wheelchair accessible, which is plus for us when we travel with family. Be sure to check the lake levels before traveling here due to the drought conditions of the lake. The swimming area was full, though, so people still were able to have a great time!

reviews.author: 匿名
reviews.text: Pros: Beautiful lake. Picturesque. Has a playground and benches. Campground within walking distance. Cons: Bathrooms are dirty. Fun area roped off for kids to play in the lake but the water isn't as clean.

reviews.author: 匿名
reviews.text: Quiet time is at 10pm. It's 1:10am and the people are very loud and disrespectful. This is not a camp ground it's a party ground. Quiet time is not enforced. Save your time and money. I've camped my whole life. This is by far the worst camp ground.

reviews.author: Jeff
reviews.text: The lake is fantastic. Beautiful and relatively warm. The trailer sites are poor. No privacy at all, kids playing on playground well past quiet hours, my truck and 21' trailer just barely fit into the site. Neighbor right on top of us.

reviews.author: 2oldies
reviews.text: Pulled in on a Monday, with no reservations. One night at a time but not crowded. Didn't need septic as a dump station provided. Can see how when crowded it could be quite busy. Nice place for families with a swimming beach and playgrounds. Very well maintained. Lots to do nearby

reviews.author: JorgyPartyof5
reviews.text: A very popular Tacoma Power park with day use area (lake), camping, hiking trail, and a dam overlook. Pluses: the lake, the hiking trail, the scenic dam overlook. Cons: not much privacy, lots of people on the weekends (to be expected in the summer), not all the RV spots have septic, if you get a non septic spot the dump station does not allow you to sani-flush your tanks.

reviews.author: Dawn
reviews.text: A very lovely park and probably best enjoyed in the off season. We spent 1 night here with little company on a Sunday in April. Even saw Mt. Ranier! Be forewarned: they were only taking cash or check when the park office was closed. We made arrangements with the park host to pay the fee on Monday morning before we left by debit card.

reviews.author: TheAdventureTravelers
reviews.text: What an amazing campground! Full hookups with pull-throughs at the base of Mount Rainier National Park. Easy access in/out for our 32' RV with the tow vehicle. Stoked to have full hookups after days of hiking. Full bathrooms with pay showers onsite as well. The lake is super-low (most are nowadays) but still beautiful.

reviews.author: camper-637894
reviews.text: Lots of pull thru spots. No internet unless you walk down to the lake which I did to read a news story now and then. Staff Ed is very nice. Great spot if you want to hang out at Mt Rainer for awhile. Ice machine has been out of service all season.
